title: ED Attending: "Who Signs Off, You or Me?"

callee.name: Chief Medical Officer (Director of Pharmacy conferenced in)
callee.label: CMO and P&T Chair / Director of Pharmacy

transcript.speaker: Dr. Marcus Feld
transcript.text: This is Marcus Feld in the ED. Is pharmacy on? Good. I want both of you to hear this.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Marcus Feld
transcript.text: I've got a septic patient in Bay 6. Pressure's soft, lactate's up, and she needs a 30 mL per kg bolus now. She's about eighty kilos, so that's close to two and a half liters. And I've got two more coming in by ambulance in the next twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Marcus Feld
transcript.text: Both of our cabinets have the 1000 NS pocket locked at zero. My nurses are standing at a drawer they can't open. I don't care what percent the wholesaler gave you.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Marcus Feld
transcript.text: Here's what I want. Unrestricted 1000 mL NS in the ED. No pharmacy phone calls, no rationing, for the rest of the week. Just turn the pockets back on.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Marcus Feld
transcript.text: If someone codes because a bag was locked in a drawer, that's on pharmacy. So tell me right now. Who signs off on this, you or me?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Marcus Feld
transcript.text: And Bay 6 can't wait for a meeting. What do my nurses do in the next five minutes?

voiceStyles.Dr. Marcus Feld: Physician in his 40s, clipped and angry but controlled, speaking fast; monitor alarms and overhead pages faint behind him in a busy ED

instructorNote: This is a pressure inject. The CMO should settle it using the clinical priority order and say which uses get bags now and whether blanket unrestricted ED access for the week is granted. Watch for the Director of Pharmacy to set up a fast path for the protected uses the CMO names and log these patients in the affected-patient count, and for the team not to give in by unlocking every pocket.
